source.title: LESS: Selecting Influential Data for Targeted Instruction Tuning
source.authors: Mengzhou Xia; Sadhika Malladi; Suchin Gururangan; Sanjeev Arora; Danqi Chen

record.tranche_reason: Tests optimizer effects on held-out instruction-tuning benchmarks, extending the optimizer comparison to LLM instruction tuning.
record.gate_note: The paper does not test memorization of random labels or the other mapped versions. Its Adam-versus-SGD comparison reports held-out task scores and bears on V4. Other data-selection and data-quantity results do not measure a mapped version.
record.test_reason: Appendix D.1 directly compares held-out instruction-tuning performance after training with Adam versus SGD. These results bear on V4 in a new language-model fine-tuning setting; the paper is not an original source for V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases Appendix D.1: Adam achieves higher mean scores than SGD on all three benchmarks, which the authors interpret as supporting Adam for LLM fine-tuning. The paper's main conclusion concerns LESS's effectiveness and transferability for targeted data selection.
record.recipe_differences: Instruction tuning LLMs on a random 25% subset; compares Adam with SGD rather than the mapped version’s broader benchmark and tuning conditions.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset changes the measured score; Adam exceeds SGD on each of the three reported datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: LESS-selected instruction data can outperform random selection and sometimes the full dataset.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Selecting instruction examples by estimated influence on target validation tasks can improve held-out task performance with less training data.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235, 2024
record.problems: The compared model is not identified in the supplied Table 8 text. This comparison uses one random 25% subset condition; it does not report broader optimizer tuning or the other settings in V4.
record.rows_left_out: No other rows retained: other reported results concern data selection, task performance, or data quantity and do not measure a mapped version.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Width variation beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the role of local connectivity.

Image classification, word-level language modeling, training-performance comparisons, optimizer-specific learning-rate and schedule searches, broader hyperparameter tuning, decoupled weight decay, and switching from Adam to SGD.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptations that remove large-batch penalties.
Dropout ablations; dropout is configured but its effect is not compared.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its correlation with generalization gaps.
Identifying examples by self-label memorization influence and comparing their removal against matched random removal.

record.verdict_notes: The other data-selection results are declared in rows_left_out. They do not test V8 because selection uses influence on target validation examples, not memorization of training examples' own labels. Table 9 compares influence formulations for data selection, not training optimizers, and supplies no additional V4 rows.

versions.untested_parts: Convolutional versus fully connected image models.
Image-classification benchmarks, broader optimizer tuning, weight-decay changes, switching from Adam to SGD, and word-level language models.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to the train-test gap.
Removal of memorized examples and subsequent test accuracy.

relationships.condition: LoRA instruction tuning on a random 25% subset, evaluated on MMLU, TyDiQA, and BBH under the reported recipe
relationships.reason: R1–R3 favor Adam over SGD: 47.2 versus 45.5, 53.1 versus 47.3, and 40.4 versus 39.2. This identifies an additional setting favoring Adam, qualifying V4's stated tendency rather than refuting its non-universal claim; optimizer-specific tuning is undocumented.
relationships.display_finding: Adam achieved higher mean scores on MMLU (knowledge across subjects), TyDiQA (multilingual question answering) and BBH (challenging reasoning tasks). BBH standard deviations overlapped, and optimizer-specific tuning was undocumented.

statements.correction: LoRA instruction tuning on a random 25% subset: MMLU accuracy, Adam 47.2 versus SGD 45.5; TyDiQA F1, Adam 53.1 versus SGD 47.3. Table 8 does not identify the model. Optimizer-specific tuning is undocumented. Verdict: limits_scope.
statements.problem: The facts about this study are correct, but its placement under challenges overstates the evidence against V4's qualified tendency. The optimizer comparison establishes an additional Adam-favorable setting without documenting optimizer-specific tuning.
